title: Neuro emergencies
summary: Time-critical neurological emergencies in the ICU: the status epilepticus ladder, acute ischaemic stroke and thrombolysis, intracerebral and subarachnoid haemorrhage, a structured approach to coma, CNS infections, and neuromuscular respiratory failure (GBS and myasthenic crisis).

topics.title: Status epilepticus ladder
topics.summary: Seizure > 5 min or recurrent without recovery: adequate-dose benzodiazepine by 5-10 min, a second-line agent (levetiracetam, valproate or phenytoin, all equivalent in ESETT) by 20-30 min, then anaesthetic infusion with EEG for refractory status.

definition.text: Convulsive status: ≥ 5 min of continuous seizure or ≥ 2 seizures without return to baseline. Refractory: continues after a benzodiazepine and one second-line drug. Super-refractory: continues ≥ 24 h after anaesthesia.

steps.title: Stabilise
steps.detail: ABC, oxygen, glucose (give thiamine then dextrose if < 60 mg/dL), IV access, time the seizure.

steps.title: Benzodiazepine
steps.detail: Lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg), repeat once; or midazolam 10 mg IM; or diazepam 0.15-0.2 mg/kg IV (max 10 mg). Give the full dose.

steps.title: Second line
steps.detail: Levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (max 4.5 g) or valproate 40 mg/kg (max 3 g) or phenytoin 20 mg/kg (fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg). ESETT: ~half stopped with each; no drug superior.

steps.title: Refractory
steps.detail: Intubate; midazolam 0.2 mg/kg then 0.05-2 mg/kg/h, or propofol 1-2 mg/kg then 20-200 mcg/kg/min (watch PRIS), or ketamine. Continuous EEG; titrate to seizure suppression or burst suppression for 24-48 h.

steps.title: Search
steps.detail: Glucose, Na+, Ca2+, Mg2+, drug levels/toxicology, CT then MRI, LP if infection possible; eclampsia (magnesium), TB/neurocysticercosis, autoimmune encephalitis.

steps.title: Non-convulsive SE
steps.detail: No return of consciousness 10-20 min after movements stop: EEG to exclude non-convulsive status.

doseCards.dose: 0.1 mg/kg (max 4 mg), repeat once at 5-10 min
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 4 mg IV, repeat 4 mg if still seizing
60 kg: 3600 mg in 100 mL 0.9% saline over 15 min

redFlags.text: Persisting coma after convulsions stop: non-convulsive status until EEG says otherwise.
Pregnant or post-partum woman with seizures: eclampsia; give magnesium sulphate.

pitfalls.text: Under-dosed benzodiazepines (e.g. 2 mg lorazepam for 80 kg) and delayed second-line therapy.
Phenytoin given too fast or in dextrose.

pearls.text: Neurocysticercosis is a leading cause of new-onset seizures in Indian adults; TB and stroke are also common.

nodes.text: Levetiracetam 60 mg/kg or valproate 40 mg/kg or phenytoin 20 mg/kg
Find and treat the cause; maintenance ASM

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ESETT 2019:** levetiracetam, fosphenytoin and valproate each stopped benzodiazepine-refractory SE in ~45-47%.
- **AES 2016:** benzodiazepine first-line at adequate dose; time-based approach.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Depth and duration of anaesthetic suppression in refractory SE are not trial-proven; ketamine use is growing.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Levetiracetam and valproate IV are widely available and inexpensive; continuous EEG is limited, so intermittent EEG and clinical vigilance are common.

quiz.explanation: Non-convulsive SE is common after convulsive SE.

topics.title: Acute ischaemic stroke and thrombolysis
topics.summary: Time is brain: non-contrast CT (± CT angiography), glucose check, then IV thrombolysis (tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg) within 4.5 h if eligible, and thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion up to 24 h. Keep BP < 185/110 before and < 180/105 for 24 h after lysis.

steps.title: Recognise
steps.detail: BE-FAST; last known well time; NIHSS; glucose (treat < 60 mg/dL).

steps.title: Imaging
steps.detail: Non-contrast CT to exclude haemorrhage; CT angiography for large vessel occlusion if thrombectomy is possible; perfusion imaging for late or wake-up presentations.

steps.title: Thrombolysis
steps.detail: Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) single bolus, or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg, 10% bolus, rest over 1 h). Door-to-needle target ≤ 60 min (ideally ≤ 45).

steps.title: Before and after
steps.detail: Lower to < 185/110 before lysis; keep < 180/105 for 24 h (labetalol, nicardipine). Not lysed: treat only if > 220/120.

steps.title: Thrombectomy
steps.detail: Anterior circulation LVO up to 24 h with favourable imaging (including selected large cores); basilar occlusion also benefits. Transfer early; do not wait to see the effect of lysis.

steps.title: 24 h
steps.detail: Neuro checks and BP every 15 min for 2 h, then 30-minutely for 6 h, then hourly; no antiplatelets/anticoagulants for 24 h after lysis; repeat CT at 24 h; dysphagia screen; glucose 140-180 mg/dL; malignant MCA infarction: early decompressive hemicraniectomy discussion (age ≤ 60).

doseCards.dose: 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg): 10% over 1 min, 90% over 60 min
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 63 mg total; 6.3 mg bolus then 56.7 mg over 1 h

redFlags.text: Neurological worsening, headache, vomiting or BP surge during/after lysis: stop infusion, urgent CT, check fibrinogen, give cryoprecipitate and tranexamic acid.
Tongue/lip swelling after alteplase: angio-oedema; stop, antihistamine, steroids, adrenaline if airway threatened.

pitfalls.text: Using the STEMI weight-band tenecteplase dose (up to 50 mg) for stroke.
Waiting for coagulation results in a patient not on anticoagulants.

pearls.text: Stroke mimics (hypoglycaemia, Todd's paresis, migraine) have very low haemorrhage risk with lysis; do not delay to exclude every mimic.

nodes.text: Thrombectomy (up to 24 h with favourable imaging)
Stroke unit/ICU care; antiplatelet when appropriate

consultantNotes.evidence: - **AHA/ASA 2026 AIS guideline:** tenecteplase or alteplase within 4.5 h; expanded thrombectomy eligibility (including large-core trials such as SELECT2, ANGEL-ASPECT); paediatric section.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Extended-window lysis guided by perfusion imaging and thrombolysis before thrombectomy in directly admitted patients remain debated.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Few Indian districts have thrombectomy; hub-and-spoke "drip and ship" and tele-stroke networks are expanding. Tenecteplase single bolus suits transfer.

topics.title: Intracerebral and subarachnoid haemorrhage
topics.summary: ICH: lower SBP to ~140 mmHg (avoid < 130) within 2 h, reverse anticoagulants immediately, treat hydrocephalus, and avoid prophylactic antiseizure drugs. Aneurysmal SAH: nimodipine, early aneurysm securing, euvolaemia, and vigilance for rebleeding, hydrocephalus and delayed cerebral ischaemia.

steps.title: BP
steps.detail: SBP 150-220: target 140 mmHg (range 130-150) started within 2 h and reached within 1 h of starting; avoid drops > 70 mmHg and SBP < 130. Smooth control with labetalol or nicardipine.

steps.title: Reverse
steps.detail: Warfarin: 4-factor PCC (dose by INR) + vitamin K 10 mg IV. Dabigatran: idarucizumab 5 g. Factor Xa inhibitors: andexanet alfa or 4F-PCC 50 units/kg. Heparin: protamine. Platelet transfusion is not recommended for antiplatelet-associated ICH without surgery.

steps.title: Neurosurgery
steps.detail: Cerebellar haemorrhage > 15 mL with deterioration, brainstem compression or hydrocephalus: evacuation. IVH with hydrocephalus: EVD.

steps.title: Supportive
steps.detail: Glucose 80-180 (avoid hypo), normothermia, intermittent pneumatic compression from day 1; no prophylactic antiseizure drugs; no steroids.

steps.title: Diagnose and grade
steps.detail: Thunderclap headache: CT within 6 h is highly sensitive; otherwise LP for xanthochromia. CTA for aneurysm. Grade with WFNS or Hunt-Hess.

steps.title: Before securing
steps.detail: Treat BP (commonly SBP < 160), reverse anticoagulation, nimodipine 60 mg 4-hourly for 21 days, EVD for hydrocephalus, secure aneurysm (coil or clip) as early as possible, ideally < 24 h.

steps.title: Days 3-14
steps.detail: Euvolaemia (no prophylactic hypervolaemia), Na+ monitoring (SIADH vs cerebral salt wasting), TCD or clinical monitoring for delayed cerebral ischaemia; DCI: induced hypertension, then endovascular therapy.

doseCards.notes: If BP drops, give 30 mg every 2 h.

tables.title: WFNS grade for SAH
tables.caption: Higher grades predict worse outcome; grade should be re-assessed after resuscitation and EVD.

redFlags.text: Sudden deterioration in SAH: rebleed, hydrocephalus, seizure or DCI; urgent CT.
ICH on anticoagulant: reversal is time-critical; do not wait for INR to start PCC if the history is clear.

pitfalls.text: Aggressive BP lowering with sublingual nifedipine (unpredictable falls).
Fluid restricting hyponatraemic SAH patients (cerebral salt wasting; hypovolaemia worsens DCI).
Tranexamic acid to prevent rebleeding: no improvement in outcome (ULTRA).

pearls.text: Spot sign on CTA predicts haematoma expansion.
ICH score (GCS, volume, IVH, infratentorial, age ≥ 80) helps communication but should not drive early DNR decisions.

nodes.text: Hydrocephalus or cerebellar > 15 mL with deterioration?
Neuro ICU care; no seizure prophylaxis

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **AHA/ASA ICH 2022:** BP target 140 for SBP 150-220; reversal algorithms; avoid platelet transfusion for antiplatelet ICH (PATCH).
- **AHA/ASA SAH 2023:** nimodipine, early securing, against prophylactic hypervolaemia and TXA.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Minimally invasive evacuation for lobar ICH (ENRICH 2024) is promising but not widely available.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Hypertensive ICH is far commoner in India than in the West and occurs at a younger age; neurosurgical and coiling access vary widely; andexanet is rarely available, so 4F-PCC is used.

topics.title: Approach to coma (GCS and FOUR score)
topics.summary: Stabilise ABC and glucose first, then look for the pattern: structural (focal signs, asymmetric pupils) vs metabolic/toxic (symmetric, reactive pupils). Record GCS components and the FOUR score in intubated patients; image early and treat reversible causes.

steps.title: Stabilise
steps.detail: Airway (GCS ≤ 8 usually needs protection), breathing, circulation; glucose; thiamine 200-500 mg IV if malnourished/alcohol before dextrose; naloxone if opioid toxidrome.

steps.title: Pattern
steps.detail: Pupils (pinpoint = opioid, OP poisoning, pontine; fixed dilated unilateral = herniation), eye movements, motor asymmetry, neck stiffness, rash, eschar (scrub typhus), bite marks.

steps.title: GCS + FOUR
steps.detail: GCS as E V M components. FOUR (Eye, Motor, Brainstem, Respiration; each 0-4) works in intubated patients and detects locked-in and brainstem signs.

steps.title: Bloods + CT
steps.detail: Na+, Ca2+, glucose, urea, LFT/ammonia, ABG/CO2, CO-Hb, toxicology, malaria smear/RDT, blood cultures; CT head; LP after CT if infection suspected; EEG for non-convulsive status; MRI later.

steps.title: Reversible causes
steps.detail: Hypoglycaemia, hyponatraemia, hypercapnia, infection (empirical antibiotics/acyclovir), raised ICP (head up 30°, osmotherapy), poisons (antidotes), seizures.

tables.title: FOUR score
rows: Eyelids open, tracks or blinks to command
Pupil, corneal and cough reflexes absent
Breathes at ventilator rate or apnoea
tables.caption: Total 0-16. Lower scores are worse; 0 with apnoea prompts brain death evaluation.

redFlags.text: Unilateral fixed dilated pupil with falling GCS: herniation; osmotherapy and urgent neurosurgical review.

pitfalls.text: Reporting a single GCS total without components (e.g. 'GCS 8' hides M5 vs M2).
Assuming alcohol intoxication explains coma (head injury, hypoglycaemia, methanol).

pearls.text: Metabolic coma usually spares pupillary reflexes; structural coma often does not.

nodes.text: ABC, glucose, thiamine, naloxone if toxidrome
Metabolic/toxic screen; CT; consider LP and EEG

consultantNotes.evidence: - **Wijdicks 2005:** FOUR score validated with good inter-rater reliability, including in intubated patients.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Common Indian causes: poisoning (OP, sedatives), hepatic and uraemic encephalopathy, cerebral malaria, Japanese and scrub typhus encephalitis, TB meningitis, stroke and hypoglycaemia.

options: Usable in intubated patients and assesses brainstem
Opioids, OP poisoning or pontine lesion

quiz.stem: Before dextrose in a malnourished patient give:
quiz.explanation: Avoid precipitating Wernicke's (do not delay dextrose).

topics.title: Meningitis and encephalitis
topics.summary: Suspected bacterial meningitis: blood cultures, dexamethasone and antibiotics within 1 hour; do not delay for CT or LP. Add aciclovir for encephalitis. In India think also of TB meningitis, Japanese encephalitis, scrub typhus, cerebral malaria and cryptococcus.

steps.title: Cultures + treat
steps.detail: Blood cultures, then dexamethasone 10 mg IV with or just before ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 12 h (+ vancomycin if penicillin-resistant pneumococcus is a concern; + ampicillin 2 g every 4 h if > 50 years, pregnant, immunocompromised, alcohol use).

steps.title: Indications
steps.detail: Focal deficits (not cranial nerve), new seizures, GCS < 10, severe immunocompromise. Otherwise LP immediately. Never delay antibiotics for imaging.

steps.title: Aciclovir
steps.detail: Altered behaviour, seizures, focal signs, fever: aciclovir 10 mg/kg IV every 8 h until HSV PCR negative (repeat if early and negative); MRI and EEG.

steps.title: Interpret
steps.detail: Bacterial: neutrophils, low glucose (CSF:serum < 0.4), high protein. TB: lymphocytes, very low glucose, high protein, ADA, GeneXpert. Viral: lymphocytes, normal glucose. Cryptococcus: India ink, CrAg.

steps.title: Add cover
steps.detail: Scrub typhus (eschar, transaminitis): doxycycline or azithromycin. Malaria smear/RDT in every febrile coma. JE: supportive (no specific antiviral). TB meningitis: 4-drug ATT + dexamethasone.

steps.title: Support
steps.detail: Airway if GCS ≤ 8, seizure control, avoid hyponatraemia, ICP measures; dexamethasone 4 days (stop if not bacterial, or if Listeria).

doseCards.dose: 10 mg every 6 h for 4 days, first dose with or before antibiotic

doseCards.workedExample: 60 kg: 600 mg 8-hourly; reduce if creatinine clearance < 50 mL/min

redFlags.text: Petechial/purpuric rash with fever: meningococcaemia; antibiotics within minutes, shock management.
Falling GCS, new focal signs or papilloedema: raised ICP or abscess; CT.

pitfalls.text: Waiting for CT before giving antibiotics.
Stopping aciclovir after a single negative PCR done within 72 h of symptom onset.

pearls.text: Dexamethasone benefit is greatest in pneumococcal meningitis (de Gans 2002: mortality 7% vs 15%).

nodes.text: Blood cultures; dexamethasone + ceftriaxone (± ampicillin, vancomycin)
Tailor by CSF, PCR, GeneXpert, CrAg; tropical tests

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **de Gans 2002:** dexamethasone reduced unfavourable outcome (15% vs 25%) and death in adults with bacterial meningitis.
- **ESCMID 2016:** antibiotics within 1 h; CT indications; adjunctive dexamethasone.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Dexamethasone benefit in low-income settings with late presentation and HIV is less clear.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) surveillance: JE, scrub typhus, dengue, HSV, Nipah (Kerala). TB meningitis remains common; GeneXpert on CSF is widely available through the national programme.

options: With or before first antibiotic dose

topics.title: Guillain-Barré syndrome and myasthenic crisis
topics.summary: Neuromuscular respiratory failure creeps up silently: monitor vital capacity and NIF, intubate electively when VC < 20 mL/kg or NIF weaker than −30 cmH2O, or with bulbar failure. Treat GBS with IVIg or plasma exchange; myasthenic crisis with IVIg or PLEX plus steroids.

steps.title: 20/30/40 rule
steps.detail: Intubate if VC < 20 mL/kg, NIF (MIP) weaker than −30 cmH2O, MEP < 40 cmH2O, or rapid decline; bulbar weakness with aspiration. SpO2 and ABG change late.

steps.title: Predict
steps.detail: EGRIS (days from onset to admission, facial/bulbar weakness, MRC sum score): high score → ~65% need ventilation within a week; admit to ICU.

steps.title: Treat
steps.detail: Unable to walk unaided within 2 weeks of onset (4 weeks for PLEX): IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day × 5 days or plasma exchange 12-15 L over 4-5 exchanges. Steroids are not recommended.

steps.title: Dysautonomia
steps.detail: Labile BP and arrhythmias; avoid large BP-lowering doses; temporary pacing for severe bradycardia. DVT prophylaxis, pain control (gabapentinoids), bowel care.

steps.title: Treat
steps.detail: IVIg 2 g/kg over 2-5 days or PLEX (5 exchanges); start or continue corticosteroids (watch for early worsening); hold pyridostigmine while intubated. Look for trigger (infection, aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, magnesium, β-blockers).

steps.title: Mimics
steps.detail: Hypokalaemia, hypophosphataemia, neurotoxic snakebite, OP poisoning (intermediate syndrome), botulism, transverse myelitis, diphtheria (still seen in India).

redFlags.text: Single breath count < 20, staccato speech, paradoxical breathing, weak cough: imminent respiratory failure.

pitfalls.text: Waiting for hypoxaemia or hypercapnia before intubating neuromuscular patients.

pearls.text: Small-volume plasma exchange is a cheaper option studied in India where IVIg is unaffordable.

nodes.text: IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days or PLEX; no steroids
IVIg or PLEX + steroids; stop trigger drugs

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **EAN/PNS 2023 GBS guideline:** IVIg or PLEX equivalent; no steroids; second IVIg course not recommended.
- **EGRIS 2010:** prediction of respiratory insufficiency.
- **International MG consensus 2020 update:** IVIg/PLEX for crisis.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Axonal GBS (AMAN) after Campylobacter is common in India; IVIg costs are prohibitive for many, so PLEX or small-volume plasma exchange is widely used.

drugs.name: Lorazepam
drugs.adultDose: 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg per dose) at 2 mg/min, repeat once after 5-10 min.
drugs.cautions: Respiratory depression, hypotension; under-dosing is the commonest error.

drugs.name: Midazolam
drugs.indications: First-line SE without IV access (IM/buccal); refractory SE infusion.
drugs.adultDose: IM 10 mg (> 40 kg) or 5 mg (13-40 kg) once. Refractory SE: 0.2 mg/kg IV bolus, then 0.05-2 mg/kg/h titrated to seizure/EEG suppression.
drugs.cautions: Accumulates in renal failure and obesity; hypotension.

drugs.name: Levetiracetam
drugs.indications: Second-line for established SE; seizure prophylaxis.
drugs.adultDose: 60 mg/kg IV (max 4500 mg) over 10-15 min; maintenance 1-1.5 g every 12 h (reduce in renal impairment).
drugs.cautions: Agitation; renally cleared (dose adjust in AKI/CRRT).

drugs.name: Sodium valproate
drugs.adultDose: 40 mg/kg IV (max 3000 mg) over 10 min; maintenance 1-2 g/day in divided doses.
drugs.cautions: Avoid in liver disease, mitochondrial disorders, pregnancy if alternatives exist; hyperammonaemia; interacts with carbapenems (levels fall sharply).

drugs.name: Phenytoin
drugs.adultDose: 20 mg/kg IV at ≤ 50 mg/min (≤ 25 mg/min in elderly/cardiac) in 0.9% saline; maintenance 100 mg every 8 h guided by levels. Fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg at up to 150 mg PE/min where available.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension, bradyarrhythmia (ECG monitoring), purple glove syndrome; many interactions.

drugs.name: Tenecteplase
drugs.indications: Acute ischaemic stroke within 4.5 h (or selected later windows).
drugs.preparationIndia: Indian biosimilar tenecteplase 20 mg and 30 mg vials are available.
drugs.cautions: Different dose from STEMI (do not use the cardiac weight-band dose). BP must be < 185/110.

drugs.name: Alteplase
drugs.adultDose: 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg): 10% IV bolus over 1 min, remainder over 60 min.

drugs.name: Nimodipine
drugs.adultDose: 60 mg orally/NG every 4 h for 21 days (30 mg every 2 h if hypotension).
drugs.cautions: Hypotension: reduce dose and split rather than stop.

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.cautions: Biliary sludge; calcium co-infusion in neonates.

drugs.name: Dexamethasone
drugs.indications: Suspected bacterial meningitis (start with or before first antibiotic dose).
drugs.adultDose: 10 mg IV every 6 h for 4 days; stop if not pneumococcal/Haemophilus or if non-bacterial.

drugs.name: Aciclovir
drugs.adultDose: 10 mg/kg IV every 8 h for 14-21 days (adjust for renal function; use ideal body weight in obesity).

drugs.name: Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg)
drugs.indications: GBS (unable to walk unaided); myasthenic crisis.
drugs.preparationIndia: 5 g and 10 g vials; very costly; check IgA deficiency if possible.
drugs.cautions: Thrombosis, AKI (sucrose-containing products), aseptic meningitis, volume load.

verify.reason: Fosphenytoin is not widely available in India; phenytoin and levetiracetam/valproate are the usual second-line options.
Tenecteplase (Indian biosimilars) and alteplase are both used; confirm local protocol and stroke-ready centre pathway.
